data.gender_notes: Eneeshay is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Eneeshay is a Sanskrit name derived from the word ‘Surya’, which means sun. This name signifies being the lord or ruler of the sun. It is a reverential name for the sun god, evoking a sense of strength, power, and brilliance. The name Eneeshay carries the meaning “Lord of the Sun” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Eneeshay usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the sun and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eneeshay total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eneeshay holds deep cultural significance in Hinduism. "Surya Namaskar," a popular yoga practice, is a series of poses dedicated to the Sun God. This practice is believed to bring good health, strength, flexibility, and overall well-being. Numerous temples and monuments dedicated to the Sun God can be found across India, further symbolizing his importance in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: For the Hindus, the Sun God is not only a divine entity but also a symbol of the individual's inner light, the Atman or the inner self. Eneeshay represents the spiritual aspect of an individual who is deeply connected to the divine energy embodied in the sun. This connection fosters peace, self-awareness, enlightenment, and an appreciation for the gift of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eneeshay: The radiant one, illuminated by the inner flame of wisdom and devotion. Embodiment of knowledge and eternal light.

historical_references.reference: Eneeshay was a revered sage and a great devotee of Lord Shiva. He is believed to have lived during the medieval period in South India.
Eneeshay is also considered to be the author of the 'Eneesha Samhita', a fundamental text for the Lingayat sect of Hinduism. This text was composed around the 13th century.
